Ask HN: How do you organize homework for a kids' coding club?

Published 2026-10-07 02:00 UTC

I run a weekly coding club for about 15 kids aged 10 to 12 at our local library, and I am looking for a lightweight way to hand out exercises and see who has finished what. Right now I print worksheets and the kids type their projects on library laptops, which makes it hard to keep track between sessions.

Most of the kids use a block-based programming environment, and a few of the older ones are starting to write simple Python. I want something that works in a browser, does not require each child to have an email address, and lets parents see progress without signing up for yet another app.

I have looked at a few classroom platforms, but they feel designed for full schools with administrators and grade books. I do not need grades. I just want a list of challenges, a way for each kid to mark one as done and show their project, and a way for me to leave a short comment.

One idea is a shared folder with a numbered list of challenges and a simple spreadsheet where each kid ticks boxes. That works for tracking but makes it awkward to share projects. Another idea is a small static website where each exercise has a page with instructions and a link to a starter project.

Privacy matters too. The library has rules about collecting information from children, so I would rather avoid anything that stores names alongside photos or projects online. Using nicknames chosen by the kids has worked well so far.

For those of you who run clubs like this, what has worked? I would especially like to hear how you keep advanced kids challenged without leaving beginners behind, and how you handle kids who miss a few weeks and need to catch up.
